'''Liao Shantao''' ({{zh|s=廖山涛|t=廖山濤|p=Liào Shāntāo}}; 4 January 1920 - 6 June 1997) was a Chinese mathematician.

==Biography==
Liao was born on January 4, 1920, to a family of farmers in [[Hengshan County]], [[Hunan]]. His father was Liao Zihao ({{zh|s=廖子豪|links=no}}) and his mother was Zeng Ping ({{zh|s=曾平|t=|links=no}}). He attended Mingde Middle School and Changsha No. 1 High School in [[Changsha]], capital of Hunan province.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://news.youth.cn/gn/201508/t20150806_6970773.htm |script-title=zh:湖南明德中学校长被查 明德中学拥辉煌校史(图)|work=youth.cn |date=2015 |language=zh}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://chuzhong.eol.cn/focus_9144/20120905/t20120905_839298_2.shtml |script-title=zh:湖南省长沙市第一中学著名校友汇总 |date=2012-09-05 |language=zh}}</ref> In 1938 he was accepted to [[National Southwestern Associated University]] and graduated in 1941. After graduation, he taught at Mingde Middle School. He moved to Peking University in 1946 as an associate professor and then to [[Academia Sinica]] as a research assistant in 1948.  He pursued advanced studies in the [[United States]], earning his [[Ph.D.]] from the [[University of Chicago]] in 1952. His doctoral dissertation was directed by [[Shiing-Shen Chern]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://tech.gmw.cn/scientist/2015-12/03/content_17949088.htm |script-title=zh:陈省身：带你“走进美妙的数学花园” |work=gmw.cn |date=2015-12-03 |language=zh}}</ref> He did post-doctoral research at [[Princeton University]] from 1953 to 1955.

Liao gave up the job that mathematician [[Norman Steenrod]] had arranged for him in scientific research at Princeton University and returned to China in 1956 as a professor at [[Peking University]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.sohu.com/a/119388197_372410 |script-title=zh:北京大学档案馆获赠廖山涛教授珍贵档案 |work=sohu |date=2016-11-18 |language=zh}}</ref>

In 1986 he was elected a fellow of [[The World Academy of Sciences]].

In 1991 he was elected an academician of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]].

==Personal life==
Liao married Wang Hongyi ({{zh|s=汪鸿仪|links=no}}) in 1942, the couple had three sons.

==Awards==
* 1982 Second Class Prize of State Natural Science Award
* 1988 First Class Prize of State Natural Science Award
